title: Grilled cheese sandwich
subtitle: Buttered bread with melted cheddar, cooked in a pan
excerpt: A grilled cheese sandwich is two slices of bread, buttered on the outside, pressed in a hot pan until the bread is golden and the cheese inside has melted into a pull-apart layer. Quick comfort food that needs only three ingredients and about five minutes of heat.
sourceNotes: American domestic tradition. The pan-grilled cheese sandwich became a household staple in the 1920s when processed cheese became widely available. Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg, covers the basic toasted cheese principle.

content.text: A grilled cheese sandwich is white or sourdough bread, buttered on the outside, with a generous layer of melting cheese inside, cooked in a dry pan until the bread is deep gold and the cheese has given way. It takes about 6 minutes start to finish and requires nothing beyond the three main ingredients.
The key detail is the heat: medium, not high. High heat burns the bread before the cheese melts. Medium heat gives both layers time to reach the right point together.

Spread {{salted-butter}} of softened butter evenly on one side of each bread slice. This is the outside. Divide the {{cheddar}} of cheddar between 2 slices on the unbuttered side. Press the other slices on top, buttered side out.
Place the pan over medium heat. Lay the sandwiches in without any added oil or butter. Cook for 3 minutes until the underside is deep golden. Press lightly with the spatula once during this time.
Flip carefully and cook the second side for 2 to 3 minutes. The cheese should be fully melted and the bread evenly golden. Cut diagonally and serve immediately.

items.fix: Use medium heat throughout. If the pan is very hot, take it off the heat for 30 seconds before adding the sandwich.

items.cause: Cheese grated too thick or in big slices, preventing even heat transfer.
items.fix: Grate the cheese finely or slice it thinly. A mix of cheddar and a more meltable cheese such as emmental or fontina also helps.

items.cause: Butter spread unevenly, leaving dry patches that scorch.
items.fix: Soften the butter properly before spreading so it covers edge to edge. Alternatively, use mayonnaise on the outside, which has a higher smoke point.

content.text: Gruyere gives a nuttier, more complex result. American processed slices melt completely flat and make the classic diner version. Adding a thin layer of Dijon on the inside of one bread slice, or a few slices of tomato, or crisp streaky bacon turns the sandwich from a snack into a proper lunch. Sourdough gives a more substantial bite than white sandwich bread.

The grilled cheese became a staple of American school lunches when processed cheese made the melt easy and reliable. It pairs with tomato soup in one of the most widely eaten American comfort-lunch combinations. The dish is on almost every American diner menu. The simplicity is the point.
